title: Heidi II opens front to non-EMR hospital market
key_facts: Health Services Daily argues Heidi II's agentic features suit Australian hospitals that lack an enterprise electronic medical record (EMR).
Tasmania's public hospital system runs Infomedix, a digital chart viewer, rather than a full EMR; Western Australia's public system is described as a patchwork.
Heidi's approach has agents navigate screens as a human would (robotic process automation).
Governance and liability concerns make the screen-navigating agents the part administrators find most worrying.
Non-computer-use agent features include discharge summary drafting, outpatient coding help and referral letters.
The article says some health services are pausing EMR decisions because of what AI can do, and notes clinicians use Heidi unsanctioned in many hospitals.
The piece is commentary and mentions an upcoming summit with a ticket discount.
quote_evidence: The question is simply: what does this do for my clinicians and patients, what does it cost and therefore what is the ROI?
why_it_matters_hint: Commentary on how an AI assistant could fit hospitals without a full electronic record system.
notes: Opinion and analysis piece; the article text we received does not describe the Heidi II launch itself in detail (who built Heidi, release date). Lowered to 4 as commentary with no new event.
